publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Pope Leo XIV Undergoes Surgery, Lung Cancer Diagnosis Confirmed
cards.content: Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer but doctors were able to successfully remove a lower lobe of his right lung after a 90-minute surgery. The Pope 71 is expected to stay in hospital for about a week to recover. The cancer was detected during routine checks and the Pope had already announced his operation to the public.

cards.title: Japanese Journalist Arrested in Russia for Alleged Spying
cards.content: A Japanese journalist named Yuki Imai was arrested in Russia's Sakhalin region for allegedly spying on Moscow's defense capabilities. Russian authorities claim Imai gathered information on people involved in a special military operation on the Kuril Islands which are disputed by Japan and Russia. Imai was taken to Moscow and will be remanded until December before his trial begins.

cards.title: Indian Politicians Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka Arrested for Protest Site Trespass
cards.content: Two top leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested for allegedly trespassing at a protest site in Delhi. They climbed over a locked gate and crossed police barricades to enter the site. The activists were detained and appeared before a magistrate who sent them to jail for five days to help the police investigate.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Anthropic Seeks Rehearing in Appeal Against Pentagon's Blacklist
cards.content: Anthropic an American AI company is asking a federal court in Washington D.C. to rehear its appeal against the Pentagon's decision to blacklist its AI models. The Pentagon said Anthropic was a national-security risk because it refused to let its models be used for mass surveillance or lethal autonomous warfare. Anthropic's AI models help defend the nation but the company won't let them be used for those things.

cards.title: Semiconductor Stocks Stabilized Despite Recent Dip, Says CNBC's Jim Cramer
cards.content: Semiconductor stocks have been falling but CNBC's Jim Cramer thinks there's a good reason not to give up on them. He says the market is ignoring the strong demand for chipmakers driven by devices like Apple's smart home technology. Cramer highlights memory chip maker Micron as an example saying it has strong long-term agreements and is benefiting from artificial intelligence growth. He also points to Intel and AMD which make chips used in many devices. Cramer thinks the group might see a pullback but investors shouldn't dismiss the underlying demand.

cards.title: Dell CEO Calls for AI Safeguards to Prevent Harm to Humans
cards.content: Michael Dell CEO of Dell Technologies thinks artificial intelligence needs safeguards to avoid doing harm to humans. He believes technology can do good or bad things like fire heating a home or burning down a village so controls are necessary. Dell thinks governments and companies building AI tools should set limits and work together to ensure the technology is safe. He's not sure what the government role should be but he's open to discussion.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Northern Ireland Man Gets First Hearing in 74 Years with New Prosthetic Ear
cards.content: Stephen Gilbert a 74-year-old from Northern Ireland was born without an ear on one side. He recently got a new prosthetic ear that lets him hear on his left side for the first time. The prosthetic was designed and fitted by oral and maxillofacial surgeons at the Ulster Hospital a specialized service that provides custom-made prosthetics for people with birth defects injuries or cancer. Gilbert is thrilled to be able to hear someone on his left side for the first time and feels less self-conscious about his condition.

cards.title: Pope Has Surgery to Remove Lung Cancer
cards.content: The Pope had surgery to remove a type of lung cancer pulmonary adenocarcinoma from his right lung. The surgery removed the cancer and the lower lobe of his lung. This type of cancer is common and usually grows slowly. The Pope's doctors will run tests to see if the cancer has spread and if so might need further treatment. For now the Pope's recovery should be good but he'll need to avoid respiratory infections and do some exercises to help his lungs adjust.

cards.title: GLP-1 meds show promise in slowing aging process
cards.content: Scientists have found that medications for weight loss and diabetes called GLP-1 may also slow down the aging process. These medications have already been shown to help people lose weight and control their blood sugar levels but the new research suggests they could also help people live longer. The medications seem to work by targeting the aging process itself rather than just treating specific diseases. While the research is still early and limited it's showing promising results with some people's biological age slowing down by 3 to 6 years. Experts caution that it's too early to say for sure whether these medications can actually help people live longer and more research is needed to understand how they work and who they might benefit.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Climate Change Linked to Increased Skin Diseases Worldwide, Study Finds
cards.content: A big study looked at how climate change is affecting skin diseases around the world. Researchers invited 194 countries to share their data and found that over 40% of countries reported changes in skin diseases with lower-income countries being hit the hardest. Countries in the western Pacific eastern Mediterranean and south-east Asia were most affected with increases in heat rashes inflammatory skin diseases and infectious diseases.

cards.title: Nepal hit by devastating flash flood, killing at least five
cards.content: Nepal was hit by a devastating flash flood on October 11. A landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki River causing a surge of mud rocks and debris to sweep through villages in the Himalayan foothills. At least five people are missing and dozens of homes were destroyed along with several bridges. The flood also damaged three hydropower projects and disrupted electricity and telecommunications. The Nepali Army rescued 95 people including nine foreign nationals with 437 security personnel involved in the rescue efforts.

cards.title: Global temperatures hit record highs in September, reaching 16.27°C above pre-industrial levels.
cards.content: September 2026 was the second hottest September month on record with global temperatures reaching 16.27°C 1.63°C above pre-industrial levels. This makes it the second consecutive month to break the 1.5°C mark. The average sea surface temperature outside the polar regions also hit a record high while many parts of the world were drier than normal. However some regions experienced heavy precipitation and floods.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Expected to Rack Up Oscar Nominations
cards.content: A new movie "La Bola Negra" is expected to be a big contender for the Oscar awards. It's a heartwarming film about queer identity and romance made for under $17 million. The movie has already won praise at several major film festivals and has been picked up by Netflix. It's considered an underdog against the big-budget "The Odyssey" but industry experts think "La Bola Negra" could rack up a lot of nominations and even win some awards potentially giving "The Odyssey" a run for its money.

cards.title: Girls TV Show Returns for Limited Run After 10-Year Hiatus
cards.content: Lena Dunham's popular TV show Girls is returning for a limited run after a 10-year break. The show's creator writer and star announced the news with the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. The five-episode revival is set to start production in 2027.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voiced Animated TV Special "The Baddies" Hits Screens This Christmas
cards.content: A new animated TV special called The Baddies is coming out this Christmas. It's based on a popular children's book by Julia Donaldson and will feature voice acting from Welsh actor Rob Brydon and some of his Gavin and Stacey co-stars. The story is about a troll a ghost and a witch who try to steal a little girl's blue spotty hanky but they soon learn that they might not be the scariest characters after all. The special is about being brave kind and standing up to bullies and it's set to be a funny and spooky holiday treat.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Bank of America Fined $1.2 Billion for Failing to Detect Money Laundering
cards.content: Bank of America has been fined $1.2 billion for failing to detect potential money laundering and other illegal activity. The bank didn't report over $5 billion in suspicious transactions to the government including some that posed national security risks. The bank relied too heavily on outside parties to help detect and report suspicious activity rather than using its own internal controls.

cards.title: UK Economy to Grow 1.3% in 2026 Due to AI Investment Surge
cards.content: The International Monetary Fund has released its latest report on the global economy and the UK is doing better than expected. The IMF says the UK's economy will grow by 1.3% in 2026 which is an increase from its previous forecast. This is partly because of a surge in investment in artificial intelligence. Despite some challenges the UK's economy is expected to be the second-fastest growing in the G7 group of countries. However the IMF warns that inflation is rising and interest rates will likely go up which could affect how much people spend and how much companies invest.

cards.title: Royal Mail sees 400 weekly staff departures amid new delivery issues
cards.content: About 400 Royal Mail postmen and women are leaving the company every week according to the Communication Workers Union. This number has gone up since the company introduced a new delivery system earlier this year. The union says the new system is not working in hundreds of offices and is causing problems for staff including increased workloads and delays in delivering mail and parcels.
